kills.change_summary: Remove the initialized guard so SetMinSum still updates MinSum after initialization.

kills.property: Depositing twice accumulates: a user's balance equals the sum of all deposits, not just the latest one.
kills.change_summary: Replace the balance accumulation with assignment, so Deposit overwrites the caller's balance with msg.value instead of adding to it.

kills.property: A Deposit of value v credits exactly v to the caller's own balance: c.balances(msg.sender) increases by v.
kills.change_summary: Credit tx.origin instead of msg.sender, so the deposit is recorded under a different key than the caller's address.

kills.property: Depositing increases the caller's recorded balance by exactly the deposited amount (balances[sender] after Deposit equal
kills.change_summary: Replace the balance addition with a subtraction, so Deposit decrements the caller's balance (reverting if insufficient) instead of increasing it.

kills.property: After calling SetMinSum(_val) before initialization, MinSum equals _val.
kills.change_summary: Remove the statement 'MinSum = _val;' so SetMinSum never changes MinSum.

kills.property: Calling SetMinSum(v) on an uninitialized contract sets MinSum exactly to v, i.e. afterward c.MinSum() == v.
kills.change_summary: Replace 'MinSum = _val;' with 'MinSum += _val;' so MinSum accumulates the argument instead of being set to it.

kills.property: On an uninitialized contract, SetMinSum always succeeds and sets MinSum to _val; it must not revert.
kills.change_summary: Invert the guard condition so the function only succeeds after initialization instead of before it.

kills.property: After depositing an amount, the depositor's recorded balance increases by exactly that amount.
kills.change_summary: Delete the statement that credits msg.value to the caller's balance, so Deposit no longer updates balances.
